summary.short: From 19 August 2025, Tucson Code Secs. 27-20 and 27-21 govern large quantity water users (10,000+ ccf monthly). Users need Mayor and Council approval of a conservation plan before new connections or meter upsizing, stay within 120% of approved use, and face civil sanctions up to 2000% of monthly charges.
summary.long: Ordinance No. 12188, adopted and effective 19 August 2025, adds Tucson Code Sections 27-20 and 27-21 on large quantity water users. Large quantity water users may not connect to City water except under Section 27-20. Applicants projecting or reaching 10,000 ccf per month, or upsizing meters to that level, must submit a water service application and conservation plan. The Director reviews applications against criteria including efficiency, water availability, economic benefit, a 30 percent reclaimed-water offset (unless the Director sets another figure), and assured water supply; the Mayor and Council approve, deny or return them. Approved applications become binding water service contracts. Users must submit updated plans every five years. Use above 120 percent of the approved amount is prohibited, and the Director may suspend service for violations. Section 27-21 sets civil sanctions of up to 200, 500, 1000 or 2000 percent of monthly charges, rising with repeat violations or duration. After a second violation, Tucson Water may install a flow-restricting device at the user's expense. Users must repay civil penalties and costs the City incurs from their violations. Section 6 declares an emergency. The text does not mention artificial intelligence or computing facilities.

notes: Annotated from the adopted ordinance (Aug 19, 2025), Sections 1-6 as provided; the full Tucson Code is not in the document. No enabling statute is cited, so no legal_basis relation is recorded. Points for readers: (1) Sec. 27-21(A)(1) covers a first violation lasting less than one year and (A)(2) covers a violation lasting more than one year but less than two; a first violation lasting exactly one year is not covered, and similar boundary gaps exist at two and three years. (2) Sec. 27-21(A)(5) says the device is installed at the user's expense, then that the applicant will pay the installation cost; the text uses both 'user' and 'applicant'. (3) The text uses both 'sustainable water service application' and 'water service application'. (4) 'Director' is not defined or named. (5) Sec. 27-20(B)(1)(a) glosses ccf as 748 gallons.

obligations.summary: A large quantity water user may not connect to the City public water system or use City water except as provided by Sec. 27-20. Applies to new connections under the program.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to a large quantity water user as defined in Sec. 27-20(B)(1), i.e., projected or existing use of 10,000 ccf per month average annual use

evidence.quote: A large quantity water user may not connect to the City public water system or use City water except as provided by this Section.

obligations.summary: Applicant must submit a sustainable water service application, including a water conservation plan, to the Director if the 10,000 ccf per month test in B(1)(a)-(c) applies. For undeveloped property the application is due when development entitlements are sought (B(2)). The application must identify phasing, structures, nature and type of water use, and projected demand (B(3)). The application and plan are public records under the Arizona Public Records Law (B(6)).
obligations.conditional_on: Applicant is a new customer, or an existing customer requesting water-meter upsizing, meeting the 10,000 ccf per month test in Sec. 27-20(B)(1)(a)-(c)

evidence.quote: An applicant must submit to the Director a sustainable water service application, which must include a water conservation plan, if any of the following apply:

obligations.summary: The water conservation plan must include techniques and technologies that reduce water consumption, reduce loss or waste, improve efficiency, or establish use of reclaimed water (B(4)). If the location is within one mile of the Tucson Water Reclaimed Water Distribution System, the plan must include information on the cost of a connection and the suitability of reclaimed water for the facility (B(5)).
obligations.conditional_on: Part of the application under Sec. 27-20(B)(1); reclaimed-water content applies only within one mile of the reclaimed water system (B(5))

evidence.quote: The water conservation plan must include techniques and technologies that will reduce the consumption of water

obligations.summary: Director reviews properly completed applications and conservation plans, and schedules the application for Mayor and Council consideration as a numbered regular session item within two months after confirming that the elements in C(2) are completely and correctly addressed.

obligations.conditional_on: Applies at Director review under Sec. 27-20(C)(2) before Mayor and Council consideration

evidence.quote: That the sustainable water service application and water conservation plan demonstrate that the large quantity water user will undertake to use water as efficiently as is practicable
